messages:
maya: Heads-up — since ~09:10 UTC the us-west-2 shared GPU pool has persistent queue growth and tenant slowdowns. Queue length rose from ~200 -> ~1.6k over 18m, and p95 latency to model servers jumped from 180ms -> 1.1s. I think this is a combo of a noisy tenant burst and a control-plane network blip that reduced our autoscaler responsiveness.

samir: looking now — saw the same spike on the admission queue. p50 async wait went from 50ms -> 420ms. Link to grafana: https://grafana.company/us-west2/queues?from=now-30m . Seems most of the backlog is short inference (<512 tokens) but super high QPS from one tenant id.

observability-bot: Alert: admission_controller.queue_length.us-west-2 > 1000 (threshold 500) — triggered at 1783456740. Active leases: 420 (90% GPUs).

anika: can you post the noisy tenant id? I will check recent rollout/traffic generator.

maya: tenant=acme-marketing (internal alias: acme-mkt). They've been hitting a new campaign model with aggressive client-side retry. No recent infra deploys on our side around 09:05-09:12.

liam: I pulled tcpdump from the control-plane proxies — there was a 40s spike of 5xxs to the autoscaler API (AZ-to-controlplane path) starting 09:07:18 UTC. That explains slow scale-up. When autoscaler lost acks we didn't raise capacity fast enough and queueing compounded.

samir: short-term mitigation suggestion: 1) apply a per-tenant emergency soft-cap (rate-limit) for acme-mkt 2) enable fast-evict for small-batch pods in us-west-2 to free slots 3) throttle cross-AZ migration for the next 10m so we don't thrash. Thoughts?

maya: +1 to emergency soft-cap. We need to be careful with SLA but better to protect multi-tenant pool. Can we do token-bucket style at the admission layer? Example quick patch I used in staging:

```
admission:
  per_tenant:
    default_bucket: 1000
    refill_per_sec: 200
    penalty_window: 300s
    burst_limit: 800
  noisy_tenant_overrides:
    acme-mkt:
      refill_per_sec: 20
      burst_limit: 60
      penalty_window: 600s
```

liam: I can push that override via the runtime-config API for us-west-2 now. It will apply at the admission controller and should shed most of their new requests without killing in-flight work. Deploying in 30s.

deploy-bot: deploy started by liam: PUT /runtime-config/admission/overrides (us-west-2) at 1783456845.

anika: also recommend turning on short-term adaptive batching reduction for that pool — reduce max batch size from 32 -> 8 for 5m so latency per item improves and we finish queued work faster. I've got a PR ready to toggle via feature-flag.

samir: + observing a drop in queue length 2m after the override. queue: 1.6k -> 520, p95 latency down to 380ms. Good signal.

maya: follow-ups: 1) make the per-tenant emergency override an action in the oncall runbook (so SRE can trigger without a patch) 2) add a circuit-breaker that marks tenants as "noisy" if they exceed sustained qps x baseline for Y minutes and auto-applies conservative limits 3) postmortem to determine why autoscaler API had the 5xx window (network path / LB flapping).

liam: noted. I'll add the emergency override endpoint to the runbook and wire a simple webhook that oncall can hit. I will also collect control-plane LB metrics/trace for the 09:07 window.

anika: for the medium term, propose a penalty-box mechanism at admission: if a tenant causes >75% of queue growth over 10m, temporarily demote them to lower priority class with stricter refill. This keeps shared-pool fairness automatic. I sketched algo in the new fairness doc.

samir: we should also consider soft isolation buckets: reserves for small bursty tenants (5-10%) so a single burst can't starve the pool, and a burst-probation state to catch misbehaving clients and request throttling from SDK.

maya: agree on both. Action items: liam: runbook + LB traces; samir: design proposal for reserve buckets + probation flow (RFC by EOD); anika: PR for adaptive batching flag; i'll own postmortem and update runbook with emergency override steps.

observability-bot: Note: admission_controller.queue_length.us-west-2 back to 390 at 1783457160.

maya: thanks all — nice triage. We'll revisit if we see any oscillation after scaling stabilizes. :thumbsup:
